limitations: Exact1.0 and2.0.0 releases not independently authenticated.
Original means upstream SMB1Base authored streams at pinned46ff88f7d9e854db80bf8d50e5bf74340fcc64ce; no separately acquired Nintendo ROM is represented as a verified byte oracle.
The static NES column inventory executes compiled baseline6502 parser calls with authored hidden1Ups enabled, not a controller replay. It does not simulate castle loopback or transport routes.
Sequence alignments expose all literal static differences but are not approved relocation recipes; repeated empty/floor columns can have multiple equivalent alignments.
Enemy spawn groups, enemy-slot exhaustion, frenzy actors, per-world native hard flags and full runtime obstacle equivalence are not certified by the static topology comparison.
Pit/Rygar/Scrooge have no official2.02 helper-mask specification. Lance should inherit Bill only if the alternate-character contract is retained.
Current Easy/Hard mode selects behavior versions; it is not the officialFlash five-position difficulty setting.

evidence: src/expanded.s:1219 fixed speed1.5px/update, jump−4.1667px/update, rising gravity~0.09723px/update²
src/expanded_weapons.s:3 flight requires flower power; cannot be assumed for a base-character gap
Pit.reason: Ordinary higher jump supports the Samus/Ryu-like vertical policy; no intrinsic dash/second jump, so source horizontal gap/flag helpers are the conservative base-power accommodation.

Rygar.reason: Installed traversal jump is higher than Pit and ordinary Mario, but horizontal speed remains modest; use H helpers without inventing a V landing for a character whose native height already exceeds those low-jump profiles.

evidence: src/scrooge.s:115 ordinary jump is intentionally native DuckTales58px rise with release cut
src/scrooge.s:95 repeatable pogo is stronger; it still requires a separate Down+B action
Scrooge.reason: Ordinary jump is the lowest of these three; H and V support avoids requiring pogo mastery or a powerup for basic progression.

revision2.comparison_limits: Complete authored source/native records; candidate coordinate pairing is not runtime spawn/collision equivalence. Exact records remain available even when alignment/phase/maze semantics are ambiguous.
